title: Resources for Public Health Professionals | Overdose Prevention | CDC
content: Resources for Public Health Professionals Aug. 15, 2025 At a glance Access intervention resources for public health professionals. About these resources As the overdose epidemic and drug landscape continue to evolve, we must take a practical, evidence-based approach to stopping overdose, saving lives, reducing risks and related harms, and removing barriers to effective interventions. This requires that we provide care and services that respect the health and dignity of people who use drugs through efforts that focus on prevention, harm reduction, evidence-based treatment, and recovery support. The success of interventions depends on federal, state, and local governments working collaboratively with healthcare professionals, law enforcement, policy makers, employers, advocacy groups, and communities. Resources ENGAGE: Evidence-Based Strategies to Prevent Youth Substance Use Use ENGAGE to guide youth substance use prevention efforts in your community. Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs (PDMPs) PDMPs can provide health authorities timely information for a targeted response to drug overdose. Public Health and Public Safety Resources A collection of overdose prevention resources for public health and public safety professionals. Overdose Data to Action The hub for CDC's Overdose Data to Action program, including information and resources. Drug-Free Communities (DFC) Learn about CDC's Drug-Free Communities Support Program and access related resources. Public Health Considerations for Strategies and Partnerships Information on overdose prevention strategies and partnerships for healthcare professionals.
